data.name: Anunitha
data.gender_notes: Anunitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anu means ‘small’, nitha means ‘goddess’. This name is derived from the Hindu goddess Anu, who is the embodiment of grace and compassion. The name Anunitha carries the meaning “Graceful Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anunitha usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner grace and compassion of an individual.
data.etymology: Anunitha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anunitha total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

The name Anunitha symbolizes the nurturing and caring aspects of a mother and inspires feelings of tenderness and love.

historical_references.reference: Anunitha, also known as Anandavalli or Anand Nayaki, was a celebrated saint and poetess in the 15th century in the Tamil Nadu region of India. She was known for her devotion to Lord Shiva and her poetic compositions in Tamil known as 'Tirumurai'.

Anunitha, also known as Adidevatha, was a renowned scholar and philosopher who lived in the 17th century in the Karnataka region of India. She was a disciple of Saint Ramanuja and is known for her commentaries on various Hindu scriptures, particularly the Vedas and the Upanishads.
